newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross seeks $12 million to help mine victims.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross seeks $12 million to help mine victims.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) called on governments and global organisations on Friday to help gather some $12 million to improve assistance to hundreds of thousands of landmine victims.

The ICRC coupled the appeal, launched at a meeting with foreign ambassadors at the Swiss-run ICRC's Geneva headquarters, with a fresh appeal for worldwid efforts to achieve a total ban on anti-personnel mines, which it called a "horrifying weapon."

The funds would go to projects helping people crippled by mines in Afghanistan, Angola, Azerbaijan, Cambodia, Georgia, Iraq and Rwanda, ICRC Director of General Affairs Paul Grossreider told the envoys.

He said it was urgent to provide care "for those who have fallen victim to the landmines epidemic" -- which the ICRC says is killing some 25,000 people a year, mainly children, and maiming many more times that figure.

The United States and other Western countries are pushing for negotiations in the United Nations-sponsored Disarmament Conference (CD) on a global ban, but the effort has been blocked by a dispute on the overall CD agenda.
The ICRC said additional funds were needed to help child amputees, who outgrew the artificial limbs its provides every six months. For adults, the replacement period was between three to five years.

In the countries where most conflicts which caused mine victims take place, the cost of replacement -- an average of 180 Swiss francs ($128) -- was totally beyond the capabilities of the victims, it added.
